structure: Part 18, the set's own docs: every file under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/docs/, read in full (3,121 lines across 13 markdown files, not the 14 the partition expected). The folder is a README plus eight guides and four recipes. README.md carries the set's run and test commands, the exports table naming the nine pieces of journey policy the gateway wires, the served-surface reference (dashboard at the set base with health, auth, sign-out and static assets; the task-list hub and its seven rows; the shared address-book picker shell behind the destination, consignor and consignment contact pages, with its role filters, eight-a-page listing, pagination, chosen-address inset, stored copy, refused id and outage rule; the commodities list and entry sub-page; potato scope; the review section; the amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete actions; the entry guard), the three boot guards that make an obligation, its page and its binding land together, the gates on the first page increment (entry guard closed, section captions wired, flow-only keys) and the engine-sync record. obligation-model.md holds how an obligation, a group, a gate and a cardinality rule are declared in this set, the purity rule enforced at boot, registration through the set's id, and the two set-owned test modules. features.md holds the feature anatomy, page identity and maturity, the controller contract, the copy rules, how a page ends (the three controls, the overview and hub wording, buttonsAfterPrimary, amend endings), party edit, bindings, the barrels, flow-section-versus-task-row, collections, and check answers and lateness. journey-flow-and-gates.md holds the five flow sections, the seven task rows, the derived and authored gates, the flow-only keys, the hub's row rules, the whole Back-and-trail policy including check your answers, notification creation, the entry guard's rules and the section-caption map. services.md holds the one set-owned service (commodity types, categories, genera, per-line fields), the platform services the journey calls and the services deliberately removed. limits.md holds every limit with its figure: the minEntries floor and absent ceiling, the two cap declarations, the continue-enforced answers, the four vocabulary-checked answers, the 58 and 400 character text caps, the one mapper, snapshot-local positions, commodity-type reconciliation and the sibling-frame gate limit. copy-status.md records which copy is provisional and which Welsh is a machine draft, row by row for ten features. testing.md and lighthouse.md hold the suites the set runs, the allow-list drift guard and its regulation-backed assertions, the browser-test helper surface and its picker, date-picker and type-ahead expectations, the stub address book's fourteen records, the five mural use cases, and the Lighthouse targets, seed shapes, score floors and CI sharding. The four add-a-* recipes record the conventions that constrain how a field, page, section or collection may be built, and this part also claims, as gaps, the places where the docs disagree with each other (flow-only keys, caption sections, 'empty' registration modules, the one-URL Lighthouse line, the seed fixture move) or are silent (page maturity levels, dashboard paging, the eleven answers, the commodity service's clients).

claims.quote: Create a section module when its first obligation lands, not before. An empty module is a liability: it reads as coverage that does not exist.

claims.quote: An obligation has a stable UUID `id`, a path-safe `name` and either a direct `status` or an `applyTo` rule that returns scope and mandate. claims.quote: A name cannot contain `.`, `[` or `]`. The same vocabulary is used for fulfilment paths and page dispatch, so a path metacharacter makes `buildDispatch` throw at boot.

claims.quote: They carry no titles, labels, hints, legends, options, error messages, routes or template names. Copy belongs to the feature; validation belongs to the controller.

claims.quote: `assertObligationPurity()` runs in this set's gateway, [`routes-high-risk-plants.js`](../../../routes-high-risk-plants.js), before routes are added, so a display-shaped key in the model fails the server start, not a test.

claims.quote: That shared object identity is what lets the fulfilment registry check that every leaf is owned once and that grouped binding paths match each `within` chain. A structurally identical copy is rejected.

claims.statement: Each journey feature is one vertical slice of page identity, controllers, copy, templates, bindings and tests.
claims.quote: Each feature is a vertical slice of page identity, controllers, copy, templates, bindings and tests.

claims.quote: plus cross-feature constant modules such as [`timing-windows.js`](../journeys/linear/features/timing-windows.js) — values more than one feature reads, written once there rather than repeated per feature

claims.statement: The features folder has two barrels: one holding every flow page's meta and spreading every feature's routes, and one holding a frozen bundle per feature that binds a leaf.
claims.quote: [`index.js`](../journeys/linear/features/index.js), whose `dispatchPages` holds the `meta` of every flow page and whose `allRoutes` spreads every feature's routes, and [`evaluation.js`](../journeys/linear/features/evaluation.js), whose frozen `featureEvaluationBindings` holds one bundle per feature that binds a leaf.

claims.statement: A multi-page feature group holds one page identity module for both pages, one shared copy pair, one evaluation module, a folder per page with that page's controller, template and tests, and a folder holding both browser specs.
